<context query="Which loops run by default on a repository whose settings say nothing about loops (default loops, settings.loops)" template="default" budget="8000">
<section name="Conventions" source="repo" priority="1">
<document source="specs/implementation-loop/spec.md" type="spec" relevance="0.52" tokens="439">
## FR7 — Per-repo enable toggle

- `lore.repos.settings` gains an `implementation_loop` block with an `enabled` boolean.
- The setting is read through a pure predicate that defaults to disabled by omission, mirroring the `autoReviewEnabled` predicate used for auto-review. A repo that has never heard of this feature never runs it.
- The toggle lives at the top level of the settings object, not inside `dark_factory`. It confers no merge authority, so it must not be dragged behind the two-key CODEOWNERS ceremony that guards the dark-factory privileged fields.
- Disabling the toggle stops new tickets from being picked. It does not cancel a run already in flight; that run finishes normally and simply is not followed by another.
- The toggle is one entry of the **loop registry** *(added 2026-10-23)*: `LOOP_KINDS` (`libs/shared/src/domain/loops/loop-kinds.ts`) names every loop a repository can switch, with its full name, and `loopEnabled(key, settings)` reads each one's switch from its own settings block, so the Loops tab and the loops read route hold no per-loop code; code review joined it on 2026-10-23 with the top-level `auto_review` flag as its switch (specs/auto-review-loop, statement 1a), and auto merge the same day with `auto_merge.enabled` as its switch, off by omission, beside its one setting `auto_merge.min_age_hours` (specs/protected-branch-merge), spec upkeep with `spec_upkeep.enabled`, on by omission (specs/external-floor FR14.13), the daily digest with `digest.enabled`, off by omission (specs/daily-digest FR10a), and spec tickets on 2026-10-24 with `spec_tickets.enabled`, on by omission (specs/spec-tickets FR14). The implementation loop keeps `implementation_loop.enabled`, off by omission, through the same predicate.
</document>
</section>
<section name="Relevant Code" source="code" priority="2">
<document source="libs/shared/src/domain/loops/loop-kinds.ts" type="code" relevance="0.60" tokens="39">
// The loops a repository can switch on and off, in the order the Loops tab shows them. A loop added later joins this tuple and `loopEnabled`, nothing else.
</document>
<document source="apps/lore-api/src/transport/routes/loops/loops.ts" type="code" relevance="0.60" tokens="72">
/** Every loop with its switch read from the repository's raw settings. */
export function repoLoops(settings: unknown): RepoLoop[] {
  return LOOP_KINDS.map((kind) => ({
    ...kind,
    enabled: loopEnabled(kind.key, settings),
  }));
}

const PATH = "/api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/loops";
</document>
</section>

**session:re-cinq/lore** (episode) [observed]: Switching Spec upkeep off on a repository's Loops tab stops the Monday 10:00 UTC cron.spec_upkeep.tick sweep from starting weekly upkeep runs for that repository.
</document>
